subject: FinSync: live chat streaming slowdown — recovery actions & postmortem
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@finsync-pay.com>, ops@finsync-pay.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T15:02:00Z
Subject: FinSync: live chat streaming slowdown — recovery actions & ETA

Hi Jason / FinSync ops team,

Thanks for the quick flag earlier — we saw the same symptom on our side: elevated token latency on the streaming/chat endpoint used by your live agent flow between 14:48–15:22 PDT. The service is stable now and we routed traffic to a warmed fallback pool; you should no longer see stalled chunks.

Quick summary of what we did that recovered traffic:
- Routed your traffic to a pre-warmed Dedicated pool (fallback) for the 14:55–15:05 window.
- Disabled an aggressive per-request batching rule that was interacting poorly with your short-prompt distribution.
- Short-term knob: enabled prefix KV caching for your session tokens to reduce repeated KV lookups.

Immediate asks for FinSync (recommended short-term mitigations you can apply now):
1) If you can, switch the chat client to our polling endpoint for high-priority agent sessions (poll every 300–400ms) for the next 24 hours until we complete the postmortem. Polling prevents client-side stalls if streaming chunks are delayed.
2) Reduce your live chunk size to 128 tokens (was 512) for agent-assist flows — that lowers tail amplification risks.
3) Send us a sample session id (one or two) where you saw the stall so we can correlate traces.

We’ll follow up with a short postmortem and concrete config changes. Apologies for the disruption — we know live chat is critical during peak hours.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: recovery-playbook-v1.pdf (outline of short-term steps)
From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@finsync-pay.com>

Cc: ops@finsync-pay.com
Date: 2026-08-11T15:18:33Z
Subject: Re: FinSync: live chat streaming slowdown — recovery actions & ETA

Thanks Neha — appreciate the rapid response. We saw about ~30% of agent sessions hit long pauses (10–18s) where the UI hung waiting for next tokens.

We switched a canary group to polling as you suggested and that group was responsive. We’ll collect session ids and paste them below by EOD. Two questions:
- Do you need us to change anything on our load balancer or just client-side chunk/polling adjustments?
- Any expected user-experience differences with prefix KV caching enabled?

— Jason
Jason Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, FinSync
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T17:06:12Z
Subject: RE: FinSync: live chat streaming slowdown — recovery actions & ETA

On 2026-08-11 15:18, Jason Lee wrote:
> We switched a canary group to polling as you suggested and that group was responsive.

Thanks — short internal notes and next steps from engineering:

Root cause (preliminary): a combination of an autoscaler race and an unexpected change in FinSync's token length distribution caused multiple streaming workers to hit a latency cliff. The autoscaler triggered instance churn at ~14:50 PDT while per-request batching was temporarily high; that increased tail latency on the streaming pipeline (KV cache miss amplification).

Actions already taken:
- Warmed an alternate Dedicated pool and routed FinSync traffic to it to bring immediate latency down.
- Temporarily lowered the batching window for the affected service and enabled aggressive KV prefix caching for sessions from FinSync.
- Increased autoscaler stabilization window to avoid near-term churn risk.

Planned engineering follow-ups (ETA next 48 hours):
1) Full trace correlation — we need session ids to correlate customer traces with infra traces (Neha: please push the ones Jason will provide).
2) A short config change (non-disruptive): pin FinSync to a different instance class for the next 7 days while we complete capacity investigation.
3) Add an early-detection alert: monitor percentiles of chunk latency per-customer and auto-failover to warmed pools when crossing threshold.

Customer-facing mitigation guidance to include in the postmortem: polling fallback instructions, recommended chunk sizes by workload, and a one-page checklist we can give to their on-call. I attached a recovery playbook draft for your review.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diagnostic-logs-20260811.zip
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@finsync-pay.com>, ops@finsync-pay.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T18:45:00Z
Subject: FinSync post-incident summary & next steps (attached draft)

Hi Jason — attaching the draft postmortem and a short runbook tailored to your live agent flow. Highlights below:

Summary: 2026-08-11 14:48–15:22 PDT — FinSync experienced elevated tail latency on the streaming/chat endpoint causing intermittent agent UI stalls. Traffic recovered after rerouting to a warmed Dedicated pool and short-term config changes.

Impact: ~7% of sessions impacted, median user-visible pause 9–16s for affected sessions, no data loss.

Root cause (final, engineering): autoscaler churn combined with a sudden shift in token-length distribution for agent prompts, which amplified KV cache miss rate and increased per-token latency under a narrow set of worker states.

Remediations & timeline:
- Immediate (done): route to warmed fallback pool; lowered batching window; enabled prefix KV caching for sessions.
- 24–72h (in progress): pin FinSync to a more conservative instance class; add early-detection alert; tune autoscaler stabilization windows.
- 2–4 weeks: model-level kernel tuning for the agent-assist model variant + expanded canary tests for short-prompt-heavy workloads.

Customer runbook (high level):
- If you see streaming stalls: switch the critical agent cohort to polling until we finish housecleaning.
- Set chunk_size to 128 tokens for agent-assist queries that embed long context.
- Provide 3 example session IDs for us to correlate (we’ve included the exact trace ids we used in the diagnostics attachment).

Attachments included: finsync-postmortem-draft.docx (editable), recovery-playbook-v1.pdf (customer-facing checklist), diagnostic-logs-20260811.zip (traces and infra logs).

We’ll schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the runbook and the 24–72h mitigation plan. Please let me know what times work best.

Thanks for your patience — we take this seriously and will make the configuration changes low-friction for your team.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
